terms.meaning: the category of a data source, such as an official live feed or a simulation
too old to trust as current

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the source class type
sections.what: Brings in the source class type so the tables below are checked against the real list of classes.
sections.why: Keeps the tables and the class list in step.

sections.name: SOURCE_PRIORITY
sections.title: Source priority table
sections.what: Ranks the five source classes. Higher numbers win, so official live feeds rank highest and simulations lowest.
sections.why: The file comment says the highest priority fresh source wins.
sections.watch_out: Priority only decides between sources of the same freshness; a stale high-ranked source does not beat a fresh lower-ranked one.

sections.name: LIVE_CAPABLE, FRESHNESS_MS, FreshnessContext
sections.title: Live classes and freshness limits
sections.what: Names the two live-capable classes and sets how old each kind of data may be before it is stale.
sections.why: Stops delayed or historical values from being shown as live.
sections.watch_out: Historical data has no age limit, so age alone never marks it as stale.

summary: Holds the rules for ranking data sources, deciding which may be called live, and how old data may be before it counts as stale.
purpose: Keeps the trust rules in one place so the app never labels old or simulated numbers as live.
why: The file comment says only live-capable sources may be labelled live, and only while fresh and while live calls are enabled.
how: Ranks source classes with numbers where the higher number wins, lists the two classes allowed to be live, and sets freshness limits: 30 seconds for live, 15 minutes for delayed, and no limit for historical.
inputs: None at run time; the values are fixed in the code.
outputs: The priority table, the live-capable set, the freshness limits and the context type.
risks: Raising the live freshness limit would let older data be labelled live. Changing a priority can change which source is shown.
debug: If a label looks wrong, check the source class on the data and these values.
